name: Lidar-in-Fog Benchmark
description: Autonomous driving at level five does not only means self-driving in the sunshine. Adverse weather is especially critical because fog, rain, and snow degrade the perception of the environment. In this work, current state of the art light detection and ranging (lidar) sensors are tested in controlled conditions in a fog chamber. We present current problems and disturbance patterns for four different state of the art lidar systems. Moreover, we investigate how tuning internal parameters can improve their performance in bad weather situations. This is of great importance because most state of the art detection algorithms are based on undisturbed lidar data.
reputation: A niche, research-focused benchmark used in sensor evaluation studies; not a widely adopted community standard.
notes: non-LLM benchmark; small controlled-chamber dataset; hardware- and configuration-dependent results; may not generalize to real-world outdoor conditions.
